thread:
omar: Morning team — unboxed my Lenovo ThinkPad and during OOBE it dropped to BitLocker recovery asking for a 48-digit recovery key. I'm remote, can't get past setup. Has anyone seen this on a fresh corporate image?

it-jen: welcome @omar. yes, BitLocker recovery can trigger if the TPM state changed (firmware update) or if the disk was swapped by the vendor. Can you share the recovery ID shown on the screen (starts with 8-digit hex)? don't post the key itself.

omar: recovery ID: 1A2B3C4D

it-bot: Ticket INC-5522 created and assigned to it-jen. https://internal.redwood/support/INC-5522

it-jen: thanks. i'm checking Intune to see if the device object has an escrowed key. can you also boot to WinRE and run `manage-bde -protectors -get C:` if you have a keyboard attached? that'll show Key Protectors and the Recovery Password ID.

omar: i'm at the recovery screen with only keyboard. ran `manage-bde -protectors -get C:` from the recovery command prompt and it shows Recovery Password ID: 1A2B3C4D and Protector: TPM+PIN (no password listed).

security-alex: likely the vendor re-flashed the disk or updated firmware which invalidated the TPM PCRs. If we've got the recovery key in Intune/Azure AD, we can retrieve and enter it to continue. Jen, can you look up the device by serial S/N LP12345678 in Intune?

it-jen: pulling device now. found object for serial LP12345678, shows BitLocker recovery key available. fetching and will DM the key to you (not in channel).

it-jen (DM to omar): Recovery key: 012345-678901-234567-890123-456789-012345-678901-234567-890123-456789-012345-678901

omar: entered the key, system unlocked and finished OOBE. Thanks!

security-alex: after OOBE completes we should confirm Intune enrollment and that the recovery key was escrowed correctly. Omar, once you're in Windows, can you open an elevated PowerShell and run: `Get-BitLockerVolume | Select-Object MountPoint, KeyProtector` and paste output?

omar: output: `C:\ : KeyProtector : NumericalPassword`

it-jen: good — looks like a recovery password protector exists and should be synced to Azure AD. I'm going to verify the key is attached to the device object and close INC-5522.

devex-maya: @omar if you need admin for dev tools we have a different flow on Windows: we can add your account to the local Administrators group via our LAPS-approved temporary grant. File the devex admin form here: https://internal.redwood/devex/admin-request and post the id. Note we prefer to avoid long-lived admin.

omar: won't need admin now, but two quick Qs: 1) should I expect this to reoccur? 2) any steps I should run to avoid BitLocker prompts?

security-alex: 1) it shouldn't reoccur once TPM PCRs stabilize. Avoid booting with firmware downgrades or swapping drives. 2) confirm Windows Update doesn't install pending firmware that requires TPM recalibration; if vendor firmware was applied pre-shipment that's the usual cause — we'll flag the vendor. Also keep disk backed up.

it-jen: i've confirmed the recovery key is escrowed to the device in Intune and closed the ticket. adding a note to the procurement checklist to verify disk/firmware state before shipping.

omar: huge thanks everyone — all set and up to speed. Appreciate the fast help on day zero.

it-bot: INC-5522 marked resolved by it-jen.
